payload.decidability_statement: classical tame knot equivalence has a decision algorithm (cited); that gives NO decision completeness to a finite-depth action search, and contracts with motion constraints and dynamic obstacles have to be re-studied separately

items.bounded_domain: finite rational PL curves with at most 16 control nodes
items.question: can all target states be represented?
items.why: wild knots, smooth embeddings and arbitrary real input are outside the model

items.bounded_domain: the declared action dictionary up to the declared depth
items.question: can all target processes be generated?
items.why: the planner enumerates a fixed submodel; anything outside returns budget_exhausted or unknown

items.bounded_domain: the instantiated move calculus (R1, R2; R3 not instantiated)
items.question: can all semantic equivalences be proved by rewriting?
items.why: classical R-move completeness for knot diagrams is a cited theorem; this experiment does not implement it, and the move calculus carries no motion constraints or obstacle data

items.question: does the decision algorithm terminate on the declared domain?
items.why: encoding/decoding, the interval certificates, the Fourier-Motzkin separation and the bounded search all terminate; the subdivision search terminates by construction and may return not-certified, which is a declared outcome

payload.mutual_implication: A, B, C and D are not mutually implied: encodability here does not give state faithfulness for topological semantics; state faithfulness for literal data does not give process faithfulness for the continuations; and none of them gives completeness
